title: Policy retrieval spike
no_opportunity_note: Roadmap intent, no accepted opportunity. Learn mode granted on that basis.

blocks.B0L: If retrieval is good enough, the whole claims triage direction opens up. If not, it closes early and cheaply.
blocks.C1: Handlers find situational precedent without leaving the claim.
D2: It will not be shown to anyone outside the build team
blocks.D3: Nothing is sent anywhere. Output goes to the build team only.
blocks.A3: They cannot find situational precedent across three policy documents, so hard claims escalate and sit with a reviewer for days.

A4.why: Accountable for cycle time, and carrying the escalation backlog.

blocks.A5: They read three policy documents to answer one question and keep private crib sheets.
blocks.A6: The backlog grows with volume, and the escalation queue is already the bottleneck in the ops review.

A7.how: Two teams built their own spreadsheets on their own time.

categories.why: Recovers handling cost in the claims in scope.
We hold the policy corpus and the workflow; others hold neither.
Removes the escalation wait handlers complain about.

B00.outcome: Reduce cost-to-serve by 15 percent in FY26
B00.contribution: About a third of the gap, from the claims in scope

learn_mode.grant_reason: Two-week spike to find out whether retrieval is good enough to design around.
learn_mode.learning_question: Can retrieval reach 70 percent exact-source accuracy on the sample set?
learn_mode.kill_condition: Below 70 percent after two approaches, the method is wrong and we stop.
